name: Reviewed classifier CI evidence
notes: Fixed external evidence for every classifier and audit case. Search/page material is retained from the reviewed evidence packs C01, C02, C04, C05, C06, C24, C26, stable-name-examples, black-label-islay-origin, and the Glenfarclas review pack, plus the cited additions. Source-image re-reads retain the captured upstream extraction where provided, including known extraction errors; classifier judgment must still handle those errors. Empty search evidence explicitly marks local-input-only cases, not a missing provider response. Expected actions, Bottle IDs, and assertions are not used to construct this data. Standalone label-extraction evals still run against checked-in images and the live extraction model. Candidate-image observations retain valid captured tool results from CI run 39285550059, reviewed against the fixture source notes. Glendalough and Russell's Reserve source labels were visually reviewed on October 20, 2026; Ardbeg retains the exact label fields already verified by its curated regression. Direct source-page reads retain the exact captured title and, where already documented, review issue/byline/price metadata. These bounded source excerpts add no facts from expected outputs.

evidence.query: the Glenfarclas 1965/2005 Scott's Selection whisky: product title, ABV, bottler versus brand, any age/cask identifier and tasting review product details
evidence.summary: | Glenfarclas 1965/2005 (48.5%, Scott’s Selection) | Glenfarclas 1965/2005 (48.5%, Scott’s Selection)Four starsHere we have an old independently bottled Glenfarclas of approximately forty years of age. In short, a youngster… Colour: gold. Nose: waxes, hessian, mandarin peel, peach and apple skins, then a few touches of fennel and wormwood. Quite understated, very elegant, a little reserved, but this resistance to modernity can only be charming. Others would immediately have subjected it to some more or less brutal re-racking. Mouth: refined, admittedly a little bitter and herbaceous, but it all works, even if it tends to dive towards… the turf, almost like a rugby player. Finish: there are some lovely aspects, but overall it’s a little short on fruit. Comments: perhaps this lovely cask had already crossed the ‘maturity pass’ two or four years earlier. But it’s still very beautiful, of course. SGP:361 - 85 points. |
